Refactor: Extract steganography module into plugin architecture

Migrated steganography from monolithic module to modular plugin system:

- Moved from modules/steganography/ to plugins/steganography/
- Organized into focused submodules:
  - core/: Base classes, config, utilities, exceptions, analysis
  - formats/: Image (PNG, JPEG, TIFF, WEBP) and audio (WAV, FLAC, MP3) handlers
  - error_correction/: Reed-Solomon and simple error correction
  - transport.py: Format detection and routing
  - stego_plugin.py: Plugin interface implementation

- Updated CLI integration in crypt_cli.py to use plugin system
- Added get_plugin() method to PluginManager for direct plugin access
- Updated plugin discovery to include steganography directory
- Fixed test imports: modules.steganography → plugins.steganography
- Removed secure_memory dependencies throughout codebase

Testing:
- All 62 steganography tests passing (16 core + 46 format-specific)
- 100% backward compatibility maintained for CLI arguments
- All format handlers operational (JPEG, TIFF, WEBP, WAV, FLAC, MP3)

Benefits:
- Improved modularity and code organization
- Clear separation of concerns
- Easier to extend with new formats
- Plugin sandboxing capabilities available

fix: Harden parse_str prototype pollution guard against includes() bypass (#533)

* fix: Harden parse_str prototype pollution guard against includes() bypass

The existing prototype pollution fix used String.prototype.includes() to
check for forbidden keys (__proto__, constructor, prototype). An attacker
can override String.prototype.includes = () => false before calling
parse_str, completely bypassing the guard.

Replace with a regex test which is not vulnerable to String prototype
tampering.

Fixes GHSA-rxrv-835q-v5mh

Add bn254 support and expose poseidon/poseidon2 host functions (#1667)

### What

* Add bn254 support (#1615, #1628)
- A new module `crypto/bn254.rs` with Bn254 point and field types, and
expose related host operations.
  - Implement `Neg` trait for `G1Affine` (#1630)
- Update bn254 typenames and add mapping (#1645), also updated bls12-381
type names for consistency
* Add raw Poseidon, Poseidon2 support in `CryptoHazmat`, gated by
"hazmat-crypto" feature


### Why

Expose new crypto functions for protocol 25

### Known limitations

Only the raw host function exposure for Poseidon/Poseidon2 has been
added in this PR. The more elaborate setup for sponge, parameters, hash
function wrappers will be done in a separate repo
[here](https://github.com/stellar/rs-soroban-poseidon)

chore: prepend SPDX/Copyright headers to source files

Mechanical batch addition of a 2-line SPDX-License-Identifier +
Copyright header to every .go / .ts / .vue source file in the repo
(backend, web frontend, hub frontend, site, scripts, tests). Headers
look like:

  // SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-or-later
  // Copyright (C) 2025-2026 lin-snow

(or the equivalent <!-- ... --> form for .vue SFCs).

Skipped:
- internal/swagger/* and internal/di/wire_gen.go (generated)
- web/src/components/icons/* (SVG icons carry their own upstream
  attributions)
- node_modules / template/dist / web/dist / .git / etc.

A new tooling script — scripts/add-spdx-headers.mjs — drives the
addition. It is idempotent (skips files that already contain
"SPDX-License-Identifier") and supports three modes: default write,
--dry-run, and --check (CI-friendly: exits 1 if any source file is
missing a header).

The Go variant correctly handles //go:build constraints by inserting
the SPDX block AFTER the build tag's blank-line separator, so files
like internal/di/wire.go remain valid build-tagged files (verified
by make wire-check).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
